Subject: DRAFT — review for Harbourline Van Works (3 stars, not posted yet)

**3 stars — mostly because of the calendar, not the tub.**

Let me be upfront about where the stars come from: my van was off the road from October 27 to November 6, and that's what's holding this to 3 instead of 5. The actual fitout was good work, and the tub and ramp are the best part of the whole build.

The backstory, so it's clear what happened. My 2021 Transit high roof was fitted out in August: stainless tub with ramp and tether rail, 40 gal fresh tank, 25 gal grey tank, propane on-demand water heater, coin-grip floor with drain, cabinetry, dryer mount and wiring for the two outlets. $9,400 plus HST, with a 12-month workmanship warranty. All of that performed exactly as promised.

Then on October 27, mid-groom, the fitting on the hot water line let go. Water everywhere, down into the cabinet, and I had a very large dog standing in a soaking tub who could not have cared less. Moose sat in there through the entire flood like a king at a spa. I was the one screaming. His owner picked him up looking like a wet sheepdog with one fluffy half and reported that he'd never been happier, that he'd thought it was a pool party. Best customer testimonial I've ever gotten and I didn't even have to write it.

What I'm docking stars for is the calendar. Off the road October 27 to November 6. I had to cancel the rest of that day plus six bookings I'd already booked between then and when the van came back. That's money out of my pocket and appointments I had to turn away from people who'd already made plans around me.

Now, the other thing that stung wasn't the leak itself. Stuff breaks. I get that, I wasn't expecting a van to last forever. What stung was hearing "user error." When the fitting let go I was told it usually means the heater's been run dry or someone has hung something off the pipe. I have never run it dry, and there's nothing to hang anything off — it's behind a cabinet door. Finding out your van is going to be down for eleven days right after being told it's your fault is a rough way to learn it.

Full credit where it's due, though: Glenn did own it. He came back and found the compression fitting on the outlet was a cheaper one his supplier had swapped in, said that was on them, and replaced all of them on the hot side. He also knocked the $180 diagnostic fee off. That takes guts when you're the one who's going to read the review, and he did it anyway. Hence 3 stars instead of 1. Nothing personal here — I actually think he's a solid builder, and the tub proves it.

One ask for other groomers and trades: get it in writing. Get the warranty terms in writing, get what's covered and what isn't in writing, and get the fittings and parts being used specified in writing. A 12-month workmanship warranty that excludes "user error" is only as good as the conversation you had at the counter that day. I'd also want the hot side fittings specified by grade or brand rather than left to whatever the supplier had on the truck.

Tub and ramp: 10/10, dogs walk right in, the tether rail is great, and it's the best money I spent on the whole build. The downtime and the "user error" phone call are where the stars went. Van's running again, bookings are back, and Moose has been rebooked. If you're in the trade and you want a proper mobile setup, talk to Glenn — just bring your paperwork.
